```{r development, include=FALSE}
library(testthat)
```

These functions turn a wide table (one column per trait) into pieces that can be analysed one at a time: by trait and group (`w2l_nest()`, `w2l_split()`), by pairs of traits (`c2p_nest()`), or with the levels of one column side by side (`r2p_nest()`).

# Wide to long, nested: `w2l_nest()`
    
```{r function-w2l_nest}
#' Reshape Wide Data to Long Format and Nest by Specified Columns
#'
#' @description
#' `w2l_nest` reshapes a wide-format `data.frame` or `data.table` into long
#' format, then nests the result by `name` (the pivoted column identifier) and
#' any optional grouping variables supplied via `by`. Each row of the returned
#' table contains a nested `data.table` or `data.frame` in the `data` list-column.
#'
#' @param data `data.frame` or `data.table`. Wide-format input dataset.
#'   The input object is never modified: a `data.frame` is converted with
#'   `as.data.table()`, a `data.table` is read as-is.
#' @param cols `numeric` or `character`. Columns to pivot from wide to long,
#'   specified as integer indices or column names. Default `NULL`: when `NULL`,
#'   `by` must be provided and the function performs a pure nest operation
#'   (no melting).
#' @param by `numeric` or `character`. Additional grouping variables for
#'   hierarchical nesting, specified as integer indices or column names.
#'   Default `NULL`.
#' @param out_type `character`. Class of each nested subset:
#'   `"dt"` for `data.table` (default) or `"df"` for `data.frame`.
#'
#' @return A `data.table` with one row per combination of `name` (and `by`
#'   levels, if provided). The `data` list-column holds the corresponding
#'   nested `data.table` or `data.frame` for each group. Grouping key columns
#'   are never duplicated inside the nested objects.
#'
#' @details
#' **Column resolution:** both `cols` and `by` accept either integer column
#' positions or character column names. Out-of-bounds indices and unknown names
#' are caught early with informative error messages.
#'
#' **Overlap guard:** if any column appears in both `cols` and `by`, the
#' function stops with an error before attempting to melt, preventing silent
#' structural corruption.
#'
#' **Factor-free melting:** `melt()` is called with `variable.factor = FALSE`
#' so the `name` column is always `character`, avoiding unexpected factor-level
#' ordering in downstream grouping operations.
#'
#' **No side effects:** earlier versions called `setDT()` on the argument,
#' which silently turned the caller's `data.frame` into a `data.table`. The
#' input is now left untouched.
#'
#' **Memory efficiency:** `.SDcols` restricts `.SD` to non-key columns, so
#' grouping keys are never stored redundantly inside each nested object.
#'
#' @note
#' \itemize{
#'   \item Passing an empty table (0 rows) triggers a `warning()` and returns
#'         a 0-row table with the regular column structure
#'         (`name`, the `by` columns and `data`).
#'   \item `name` and `value` are reserved for the long format; `data` must
#'         not contain other columns with these names.
#'   \item `cols` and `by` must not overlap; overlapping columns will raise
#'         an error.
#'   \item `out_type` values other than `"dt"` or `"df"` raise an error.
#' }
#'
#' @seealso `tidytable::nest_by()` for a tidyverse-style equivalent.
#'
#' @import data.table
#' @export
w2l_nest <- function(data, cols = NULL, by = NULL, out_type = "dt") {

  # -- 1. Input validation ----------------------------------------------------
  if (!is.data.frame(data))
    stop("`data` must be a data.frame or a data.table.", call. = FALSE)
  .check_choice(out_type, c("dt", "df"), "out_type")

  # Never touch the caller's object: setDT() would change its class by
  # reference. as.data.table() is only called for non-data.table input;
  # a data.table is used as-is because nothing below modifies it.
  dt <- if (data.table::is.data.table(data)) data else data.table::as.data.table(data)
  data_names <- names(dt)

  # -- 2. Resolve columns -----------------------------------------------------
  by <- .resolve_cols(by, data_names, "by", allow_null = TRUE)
  if (is.null(cols)) {
    if (is.null(by))
      stop("When `cols` is NULL, `by` must be provided.", call. = FALSE)
  } else {
    cols  <- .resolve_cols(cols, data_names, "cols")
    overlap <- intersect(cols, by)
    if (length(overlap) > 0L)
      stop("`cols` and `by` share column(s), which would corrupt the melt structure: ",
           paste(overlap, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
    if (any(c("name", "value") %chin% setdiff(data_names, cols)))
      stop("`data` already contains a column named 'name' or 'value' that is not ",
           "in `cols`; rename it first, as these names are used for the long format.",
           call. = FALSE)
  }

  # -- 3. Empty input: return a 0-row table with the regular structure --------
  if (nrow(dt) == 0L) {
    warning("`data` has 0 rows; returning an empty nested data.table.", call. = FALSE)
    out <- c(if (!is.null(cols)) list(name = character(0L)),
             if (length(by)) as.list(dt[0L, by, with = FALSE]),
             list(data = list()))
    return(data.table::setDT(out)[])
  }

  # -- 4. Pure nest mode (no melting) -----------------------------------------
  if (is.null(cols)) {
    return(.nest_by_group(dt, group_by = by,
                          sd_cols = setdiff(data_names, by),
                          out_type = out_type))
  }

  # -- 5. Wide-to-long, then nest by name (+ by) ------------------------------
  melted <- data.table::melt(
    dt,
    measure.vars    = cols,
    variable.name   = "name",
    value.name      = "value",
    variable.factor = FALSE
  )
  group_keys <- c("name", by)
  .nest_by_group(melted, group_by = group_keys,
                 sd_cols = setdiff(names(melted), group_keys),
                 out_type = out_type)
}
```
  
```{r example-w2l_nest}
# Example: Wide to long format nesting demonstrations

# Example 1: Basic nesting by group
w2l_nest(
  data = iris,                    # Input dataset
  by = "Species"                  # Group by Species column
)

# Example 2: Nest specific columns with numeric indices
w2l_nest(
  data = iris,                    # Input dataset
  cols = 1:4,                   # Select first 4 columns to nest
  by = "Species"                  # Group by Species column
)

# Example 3: Nest specific columns with column names
w2l_nest(
  data = iris,                    # Input dataset
  cols = c("Sepal.Length",        # Select columns by name
           "Sepal.Width",
           "Petal.Length"),
  by = 5                          # Group by column index 5 (Species)
)
# Returns similar structure to Example 2
```

```{r tests-w2l_nest}
test_that("w2l_nest does not modify the caller's data.frame", {
  df <- data.frame(a = 1:2, b = 3:4, g = c("x", "y"))
  w2l_nest(df, cols = 1:2, by = "g")
  expect_identical(class(df), "data.frame")
  w2l_nest(iris, by = "Species")
  expect_identical(class(iris), "data.frame")
})

test_that("w2l_nest returns the expected structure", {
  res <- w2l_nest(iris, cols = 1:2, by = "Species")
  expect_identical(names(res), c("name", "Species", "data"))
  expect_equal(nrow(res), 6L)
  expect_identical(names(res$data[[1]]), c("Petal.Length", "Petal.Width", "value"))
  expect_s3_class(w2l_nest(iris, cols = 1, by = 5, out_type = "df")$data[[1]],
                  "data.frame", exact = TRUE)
})

test_that("w2l_nest empty input keeps the regular structure", {
  expect_warning(res <- w2l_nest(iris[0, ], cols = 1:2, by = "Species"), "0 rows")
  expect_identical(names(res), c("name", "Species", "data"))
  expect_equal(nrow(res), 0L)
})

test_that("w2l_nest validates its arguments", {
  expect_error(w2l_nest(iris), "`by` must be provided")
  expect_error(w2l_nest(iris, cols = 5, by = 5), "share column")
  expect_error(w2l_nest(iris, by = 5, out_type = "x"), "out_type")
  expect_error(w2l_nest(1:3, by = 1), "data.frame")
})
```

```{r function-.nest_by_group}
#' Nest a data.table by group (internal)
#'
#' Shared by w2l_nest() and c2p_nest(). `group_by` may be NULL (one group).
#'
#' @param dt        A data.table ready for nesting.
#' @param group_by  Character vector of grouping columns, or NULL.
#' @param sd_cols   Columns stored inside each nested object.
#' @param out_type "dt" or "df".
#' @return A data.table with the group keys and a `data` list-column.
#' @noRd
.nest_by_group <- function(dt, group_by, sd_cols, out_type) {
  . <- NULL
  if (out_type == "dt") {
    dt[, .(data = list(.SD)), by = group_by, .SDcols = sd_cols]
  } else {
    # .SD is a re-used buffer inside grouping, so a copy is required anyway;
    # setDF() then converts that private copy in place.
    dt[, .(data = list(data.table::setDF(data.table::copy(.SD)))),
       by = group_by, .SDcols = sd_cols]
  }
}
```

# Wide to long, split into a list: `w2l_split()`
    
```{r function-w2l_split}
#' Reshape Wide Data to Long Format and Split into a Named List
#'
#' @description
#' `w2l_split` reshapes a wide-format `data.frame` or `data.table` into long
#' format, then splits the result into a named list keyed by the pivoted column
#' identifier (`variable`) and any optional grouping variables supplied via
#' `by`. List element names are derived directly from the grouping key
#' combinations produced by `split()`, guaranteeing name-to-content alignment.
#'
#' @param data `data.frame` or `data.table`. Wide-format input dataset.
#'   The input object is never modified.
#' @param cols `numeric` or `character`. Columns to pivot from wide to long,
#'   specified as integer indices or column names. Default `NULL`: when `NULL`,
#'   `by` must be provided and the function splits the data as-is without
#'   melting.
#' @param by `numeric` or `character`. Additional grouping variables used as
#'   secondary split keys, specified as integer indices or column names.
#'   Default `NULL`.
#' @param out_type `character`. Class of each list element: `"dt"` for
#'   `data.table` (default) or `"df"` for `data.frame`.
#' @param sep `character`. Separator used when concatenating multiple grouping
#'   key values into a single list-element name. Default `"_"`.
#'
#' @return A named list of `data.table` or `data.frame` objects (controlled by
#'   `out_type`). Names reflect the key combination of `variable` (and `by`
#'   levels if provided), joined by `sep`.
#' \itemize{
#'   \item If `by` is `NULL`, the list is keyed by the pivoted column names only.
#'   \item If `by` is specified, the list is keyed by `variable` and all `by`
#'         level combinations.
#' }
#'
#' @details
#' **Name safety:** list names are built from each element's own key values
#' (joined by `sep`), so names always match contents. This also makes `sep`
#' work on every data.table version (`split(sep = )` is only honoured from
#' data.table 1.16.0 on). If two groups would get the same name (key values
#' that themselves contain `sep`, e.g. `"a_b" + "c"` and `"a" + "b_c"`), an
#' error is raised; choose a `sep` that does not occur in the key values.
#'
#' **Column resolution:** both `cols` and `by` accept integer column
#' positions or character column names. Out-of-bounds indices and unknown names
#' are caught early with informative error messages.
#'
#' **Overlap guard:** columns appearing in both `cols` and `by` raise an
#' error before melting to prevent `id.vars` / `measure.vars` conflicts.
#'
#' **Factor-free melting:** `melt()` is called with `variable.factor = FALSE`
#' so the `variable` column is always `character`, keeping `split()` sort order
#' consistent with lexicographic expectations.
#'
#' **Memory efficiency:** the elements returned by `split()` are independent
#' objects, so for `out_type = "df"` they are converted in place with
#' `setDF()` and no column vector is duplicated. The input itself is never
#' modified.
#'
#' @note
#' \itemize{
#'   \item An empty input table (0 rows) triggers a `warning()` and returns an
#'         empty list immediately.
#'   \item `cols` and `by` must not overlap; shared columns raise an error.
#'   \item `out_type` values other than `"dt"` or `"df"` raise an error.
#' }
#'
#' @seealso `tidytable::group_split()` for a tidyverse-style equivalent.
#'
#' @import data.table
#' @export
w2l_split <- function(data, cols = NULL, by = NULL, out_type = "dt", sep = "_") {

  # -- 1. Input validation ----------------------------------------------------
  if (!is.data.frame(data))
    stop("`data` must be a data.frame or a data.table.", call. = FALSE)
  .check_choice(out_type, c("dt", "df"), "out_type")
  if (!is.character(sep) || length(sep) != 1L || is.na(sep))
    stop("`sep` must be a single character string.", call. = FALSE)

  # Never modify the caller's object (see w2l_nest()).
  dt <- if (data.table::is.data.table(data)) data else data.table::as.data.table(data)
  data_names <- names(dt)

  # -- 2. Resolve columns -----------------------------------------------------
  by <- .resolve_cols(by, data_names, "by", allow_null = TRUE)
  if (is.null(cols)) {
    if (is.null(by))
      stop("When `cols` is NULL, `by` must be provided.", call. = FALSE)
  } else {
    cols  <- .resolve_cols(cols, data_names, "cols")
    overlap <- intersect(cols, by)
    if (length(overlap) > 0L)
      stop("`cols` and `by` share column(s), which would corrupt the melt structure: ",
           paste(overlap, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
    if (any(c("variable", "value") %chin% setdiff(data_names, cols)))
      stop("`data` already contains a column named 'variable' or 'value' that is ",
           "not in `cols`; rename it first.", call. = FALSE)
  }

  # -- 3. Empty input ---------------------------------------------------------
  if (nrow(dt) == 0L) {
    warning("`data` has 0 rows; returning an empty list.", call. = FALSE)
    return(list())
  }

  # -- 4. Split as-is (no melting) --------------------------------------------
  if (is.null(cols)) {
    return(.convert_split_type(.split_named(dt, by, sep), out_type))
  }

  # -- 5. Wide-to-long, then split by variable (+ by) -------------------------
  dt_long <- data.table::melt(
    dt,
    measure.vars    = cols,
    variable.name   = "variable",
    value.name      = "value",
    variable.factor = FALSE
  )
  .convert_split_type(.split_named(dt_long, c("variable", by), sep), out_type)
}
```
  
```{r example-w2l_split}
# Example: Wide to long format splitting demonstrations

# Example 1: Basic splitting by Species
w2l_split(
  data = iris,                    # Input dataset
  by = "Species"                  # Split by Species column
) |> 
  lapply(head)                    # Show first 6 rows of each split

# Example 2: Split specific columns using numeric indices
w2l_split(
  data = iris,                    # Input dataset
  cols = 1:3,                   # Select first 3 columns to split
  by = 5                          # Split by column index 5 (Species)
) |> 
  lapply(head)                    # Show first 6 rows of each split

# Example 3: Split specific columns using column names
list_res <- w2l_split(
  data = iris,                    # Input dataset
  cols = c("Sepal.Length",        # Select columns by name
           "Sepal.Width"),
  by = "Species"                  # Split by Species column
)
lapply(list_res, head)            # Show first 6 rows of each split
# Returns similar structure to Example 2
```

```{r tests-w2l_split}
test_that("w2l_split names match the content of each element", {
  res <- w2l_split(mtcars, cols = "mpg", by = c("am", "vs"), sep = "|")
  for (nm in names(res)) {
    k <- strsplit(nm, "|", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
    expect_true(all(mtcars$mpg[mtcars$am == k[2] & mtcars$vs == k[3]] %in% res[[nm]]$value))
  }
  expect_false(any(c("variable", "am", "vs") %in% names(res[[1]])))
})

test_that("w2l_split honours out_type and leaves the input untouched", {
  df <- data.frame(a = 1:4, g = c("x", "x", "y", "y"))
  res <- w2l_split(df, by = "g", out_type = "df")
  expect_identical(names(res), c("x", "y"))
  expect_s3_class(res$x, "data.frame", exact = TRUE)
  expect_identical(class(df), "data.frame")
})

test_that("w2l_split stops when list names would be duplicated", {
  d <- data.frame(a = c("x_y", "x"), b = c("z", "y_z"), v = 1:2)
  expect_error(w2l_split(d, by = c("a", "b")), "same list name")
  expect_named(w2l_split(d, by = c("a", "b"), sep = "|"), c("x_y|z", "x|y_z"))
})
```


```{r function-.convert_split_type}
#' Convert the elements of a split() result to the requested class (internal)
#'
#' @param dt_list    Named list of data.tables produced by split().
#' @param out_type "dt" or "df".
#' @return The same named list with elements of the requested class.
#' @noRd
.convert_split_type <- function(dt_list, out_type) {
  if (out_type == "df") {
    # Elements returned by split() are independent objects, so they can be
    # converted in place with setDF(): no column vector is duplicated.
    dt_list <- lapply(dt_list, data.table::setDF)
  }
  dt_list
}
```

```{r function-.split_named}
#' Split a data.table by key columns with names joined by `sep` (internal)
#'
#' @param dt   A data.table.
#' @param keys Character vector of key columns (dropped from each element).
#' @param sep  Separator used to join key values into element names.
#' @return A named list of data.tables.
#' @noRd
.split_named <- function(dt, keys, sep) {
  # `sep =` is only honoured by split.data.table() from data.table 1.16.0 on
  # (older versions silently use "."). Names are therefore built here from
  # each element's own key values, which also guarantees name/content
  # alignment regardless of the data.table version.
  lst <- split(dt, by = keys, keep.by = TRUE, drop = TRUE, sorted = FALSE)
  nms <- vapply(lst, function(x) {
    paste(vapply(keys, function(k) as.character(x[[k]][1L]), character(1L)),
          collapse = sep)
  }, character(1L))
  if (anyDuplicated(nms)) {
    dup <- unique(nms[duplicated(nms)])
    stop("Different groups would get the same list name (",
         paste(utils::head(dup, 5L), collapse = ", "),
         "): the key values contain `sep` (\"", sep, "\"). ",
         "Choose a `sep` that does not occur in the `by` values.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  # Elements are independent objects: drop the key columns by reference.
  lst <- lapply(lst, function(x) data.table::set(x, j = keys, value = NULL))
  names(lst) <- nms
  lst
}
```

# All pairs of columns: `c2p_nest()`
    
```{r function-c2p_nest}
#' Column to Pair Nested Transformation
#'
#' @description
#' Generates combinations of specified columns and creates a nested data
#' structure based on these pairs. Each nested subset renames the combined
#' columns to \code{value1}, \code{value2}, ... (up to \code{pairs_n}) to
#' support uniform iterative analyses such as genetic correlation estimation.
#'
#' @param data A data.frame or data.table to be transformed.
#' @param cols A character vector of column names or a numeric vector of
#'   column indices to be combined into pairs. Must not overlap with \code{by}.
#'   Duplicated entries are removed with a warning.
#' @param by A character vector of column names or a numeric vector of column
#'   indices to group by. Default is \code{NULL}.
#' @param pairs_n A positive integer >= 2 indicating the size of each column
#'   combination (e.g., 2 for pairwise). Default is \code{2}.
#' @param sep A single character string used as a separator when constructing
#'   the \code{pairs} identifier column. Default is \code{"-"}.
#' @param out_type A character string specifying the class of each nested
#'   object: \code{"dt"} (data.table, default) or \code{"df"} (data.frame).
#'
#' @details
#' The columns specified in \code{cols} are renamed to \code{value1},
#' \code{value2}, ... within each nested subset. The original column names are
#' preserved in the \code{pairs} column (e.g., \code{"Sepal.Length-Sepal.Width"}),
#' ensuring full traceability for downstream iterative analyses such as genetic
#' correlation estimation.
#'
#' Columns that belong to neither \code{cols} nor \code{by} (referred to
#' internally as "extra columns") are retained inside the nested subsets so
#' that covariates or ID fields remain accessible. Grouping columns (\code{by})
#' are \emph{not} duplicated inside the nested data because they are already
#' present as outer key columns in the returned table.
#'
#' When the number of requested combinations exceeds 500 a message is emitted;
#' above 5000 a warning is raised, as memory usage grows linearly with the
#' combination count.
#'
#' The names \code{value1}, \code{value2}, ..., \code{pairs} and
#' \code{data} are reserved: \code{data} must not contain other columns
#' with these names. The input object is never modified.
#'
#' @return A \code{data.table} with columns:
#' \describe{
#'   \item{pairs}{Character. The column-combination identifier, e.g.
#'     \code{"Sepal.Length-Sepal.Width"}.}
#'   \item{...}{Any \code{by} grouping columns, one per variable.}
#'   \item{data}{List-column. Each cell holds a data.table (or data.frame when
#'     \code{out_type = "df"}) containing \code{value1}, \code{value2}, ...,
#'     plus any extra columns that were neither in \code{cols} nor
#'     \code{by}.}
#' }
#'
#' @seealso \code{\link[utils]{combn}} for the underlying combination generator.
#'
#' @import data.table
#' @importFrom utils combn
#' @export
c2p_nest <- function(data,
                     cols,
                     by       = NULL,
                     pairs_n  = 2L,
                     sep      = "-",
                     out_type = "dt") {
  pairs <- NULL

  # -- 1. Validate inputs -----------------------------------------------------
  if (!is.data.frame(data))
    stop("`data` must be a data.table or data.frame.", call. = FALSE)
  # Read-only use below, so a data.table input needs no copy.
  dt <- if (data.table::is.data.table(data)) data else data.table::as.data.table(data)

  cols <- .resolve_cols(cols, names(dt), "cols")   # also de-duplicates
  by        <- .resolve_cols(by, names(dt), "by", allow_null = TRUE)

  overlap <- intersect(cols, by)
  if (length(overlap) > 0L)
    stop("Column(s) appear in both `cols` and `by`: ",
         paste(overlap, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)

  pairs_n <- .check_count(pairs_n, "pairs_n", 2L)
  if (pairs_n > length(cols))
    stop(sprintf("`pairs_n` (%d) cannot exceed the number of `cols` columns (%d).",
                 pairs_n, length(cols)), call. = FALSE)
  if (!is.character(sep) || length(sep) != 1L || is.na(sep))
    stop("`sep` must be a single character string.", call. = FALSE)
  .check_choice(out_type, c("dt", "df"), "out_type")

  extra_cols  <- setdiff(names(dt), c(cols, by))
  value_names <- paste0("value", seq_len(pairs_n))

  # Reserved names would collide with the renamed / generated columns.
  clash <- c(intersect(extra_cols, value_names),
             intersect(c(by, extra_cols), c("pairs", "data")))
  if (length(clash) > 0L)
    stop("`data` contains column(s) whose names are reserved by c2p_nest(): ",
         paste(unique(clash), collapse = ", "), ". Please rename them first.",
         call. = FALSE)

  # -- 2. Combination count guard ---------------------------------------------
  n_combs <- choose(length(cols), pairs_n)
  if (n_combs > 5000) {
    warning(sprintf(paste0("%.0f combinations requested. Memory usage will be high - ",
                           "consider reducing `cols` or `pairs_n`."), n_combs),
            call. = FALSE)
  } else if (n_combs > 500) {
    message(sprintf("Note: generating %.0f combinations - this may take a moment.",
                    n_combs))
  }

  # -- 3. One nested table per combination ------------------------------------
  comb_list <- utils::combn(cols, pairs_n, simplify = FALSE)

  nested_list <- lapply(comb_list, function(comb) {
    # Column selection with `with = FALSE` already returns a new table, so
    # renaming it never touches `dt`; no extra copy() is needed.
    dt_sub <- dt[, c(by, extra_cols, comb), with = FALSE]
    data.table::setnames(dt_sub, comb, value_names)
    res <- .nest_by_group(dt_sub, group_by = by,
                          sd_cols = setdiff(names(dt_sub), by),
                          out_type = out_type)
    res[, pairs := paste(comb, collapse = sep)]
    res
  })

  # -- 4. Combine; order: pairs, by..., data ----------------------------------
  result <- data.table::rbindlist(nested_list, use.names = TRUE)
  data.table::setcolorder(result, c("pairs", by, "data"))
  result[]
}
```


```{r example-c2p_nest}
# Example data preparation: Define column names for combination
col_names <- c("Sepal.Length", "Sepal.Width", "Petal.Length")

# Example 1: Basic column-to-pairs nesting with custom separator
c2p_nest(
  iris,                   # Input iris dataset
  cols = col_names,       # Columns to be combined as pairs
  pairs_n = 2,            # Create pairs of 2 columns
  sep = "&"               # Custom separator for pair names
)
# Returns a nested data.table where:
# - pairs: combined column names (e.g., "Sepal.Length&Sepal.Width")
# - data: list column containing data.tables with value1, value2 columns

# Example 2: Column-to-pairs nesting with numeric indices and grouping
c2p_nest(
  iris,                   # Input iris dataset
  cols = 1:3,             # First 3 columns to be combined
  pairs_n = 2,            # Create pairs of 2 columns
  by = 5                  # Group by 5th column (Species)
)
# Returns a nested data.table where:
# - pairs: combined column names
# - Species: grouping variable
# - data: list column containing data.tables grouped by Species
```

```{r tests-c2p_nest}
test_that("c2p_nest builds every combination with renamed value columns", {
  res <- c2p_nest(iris, cols = 1:3, by = "Species")
  expect_equal(nrow(res), 3L * 3L)
  expect_identical(names(res), c("pairs", "Species", "data"))
  expect_true(all(c("value1", "value2") %in% names(res$data[[1]])))
  expect_false("Species" %in% names(res$data[[1]]))
})

test_that("c2p_nest never renames columns of the input data.table", {
  dt <- data.table::as.data.table(iris)
  before <- data.table::copy(names(dt))
  c2p_nest(dt, cols = 1:3)
  expect_identical(names(dt), before)
})

test_that("c2p_nest validates its arguments", {
  expect_warning(c2p_nest(iris, cols = c(1, 1, 2)), "duplicated")
  df <- data.frame(a = 1, b = 2, value1 = 3)
  expect_error(c2p_nest(df, cols = c("a", "b")), "reserved")
  expect_error(c2p_nest(iris, cols = 1:2, pairs_n = 3), "cannot exceed")
})
```

# Levels of a column side by side: `r2p_nest()`
    
```{r function-r2p_nest}
#' Row to Pair Nested Transformation
#'
#' @description
#' Pivots the levels of one column (`names_from`, e.g. environment, farm or
#' test station) into separate columns for every trait in `cols`, aligning
#' records by the identifier columns `id` (e.g. the animal ID). The result is
#' nested by trait, ready for iterative analyses such as genetic correlations
#' of the same trait across environments.
#'
#' @param data Input `data.frame` or `data.table`. It is never modified.
#' @param names_from A single column name or index whose levels become columns.
#' @param cols A character vector of column names or numeric indices: the
#'   trait columns to pivot.
#' @param id Identifier column(s) used to align rows across levels of
#'   `names_from`. Default `NULL` uses all columns that are neither in `cols`
#'   nor `names_from` (a message lists them); supplying `id` explicitly is
#'   strongly recommended.
#' @param out_type Output nesting format (`"dt"` or `"df"`). Default `"dt"`.
#'
#' @details
#' The combination of `id` and `names_from` must identify every row uniquely.
#' Otherwise `dcast()` would aggregate duplicated records with `length()` and
#' silently replace trait values by counts; the function stops instead.
#'
#' Other trait columns in `cols` are never used as identifiers: their values
#' differ between environments and would prevent any pairing.
#'
#' @return A nested `data.table` with columns `name` (trait) and `data`.
#'   Each nested table holds the `id` columns plus one column per level of
#'   `names_from`.
#'
#' @import data.table
#' @importFrom stats as.formula
#' @export
r2p_nest <- function(data,
                     names_from,
                     cols,
                     out_type = "dt",
                     id       = NULL) {

  # -- 1. Validate inputs -----------------------------------------------------
  if (!is.data.frame(data))
    stop("`data` must be a data.table or data.frame.", call. = FALSE)

  # dcast() returns new objects, so the input is never modified: no copy.
  dt <- if (data.table::is.data.table(data)) data else data.table::as.data.table(data)
  nms <- names(dt)

  names_from <- .resolve_cols(names_from, nms, "names_from")
  if (length(names_from) != 1L)
    stop("`names_from` must be a single column.", call. = FALSE)
  cols <- .resolve_cols(cols, nms, "cols")
  if (names_from %chin% cols)
    stop("`names_from` must not also appear in `cols`.", call. = FALSE)
  .check_choice(out_type, c("dt", "df"), "out_type")

  # -- 2. Identifier columns ----------------------------------------------------
  # Rows are aligned across levels of `names_from` by `id`. Other trait columns
  # must never act as identifiers: they differ between environments and would
  # prevent any pairing.
  if (is.null(id)) {
    id <- setdiff(nms, c(cols, names_from))
    if (length(id) > 0L)
      message("[ r2p_nest ] `id` not supplied; using all remaining column(s) as ",
              "identifiers: ", paste(id, collapse = ", "),
              ". Supply `id` explicitly (e.g. the animal ID) for reliable pairing.")
  } else {
    id <- .resolve_cols(id, nms, "id")
    overlap <- intersect(id, c(cols, names_from))
    if (length(overlap) > 0L)
      stop("`id` must not overlap with `cols` or `names_from`: ",
           paste(overlap, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
  }
  if (length(id) == 0L)
    stop("No identifier column available; supply `id`.", call. = FALSE)

  # Without uniqueness dcast() would silently aggregate with length(),
  # replacing trait values by counts.
  if (anyDuplicated(dt, by = c(id, names_from)) > 0L)
    stop("The combination of `id` (", paste(id, collapse = ", "), ") and `names_from` (",
         names_from, ") does not uniquely identify rows; dcast() would aggregate ",
         "values into counts. Check for duplicated records or supply a more ",
         "specific `id`.", call. = FALSE)

  if (anyNA(dt[[names_from]]))
    warning("`names_from` (", names_from, ") contains NA; those rows become a ",
            "column named 'NA' in every nested table.", call. = FALSE)
  clash <- intersect(as.character(unique(dt[[names_from]])), id)
  if (length(clash) > 0L)
    stop("Value(s) of `names_from` coincide with `id` column name(s): ",
         paste(clash, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)

  form <- stats::as.formula(sprintf(
    "%s ~ %s",
    paste(sprintf("`%s`", id), collapse = " + "),
    sprintf("`%s`", names_from)
  ))

  # -- 3. Pivot each trait --------------------------------------------------------
  result_list <- lapply(cols, function(b) {
    wide <- data.table::dcast(dt, form, value.var = b)
    if (out_type == "df") data.table::setDF(wide)
    res <- data.table::data.table(name = b)
    res[, data := list(list(wide))]
    res
  })

  data.table::rbindlist(result_list)
}
```

```{r example-r2p_nest}
# Example: the same traits recorded on the same animals in two farms
set.seed(1)
growth <- data.frame(
  animal = rep(sprintf("A%02d", 1:6), each = 2),
  farm   = rep(c("farm1", "farm2"), times = 6),
  adg    = round(rnorm(12, 900, 50)),     # average daily gain
  bf     = round(rnorm(12, 11, 1.5), 1)   # backfat
)

# Example 1: column names
r2p_nest(
  growth,
  names_from = "farm",           # levels become columns: farm1, farm2
  cols      = c("adg", "bf"),    # traits to pivot
  id        = "animal"           # aligns records of the same animal
)
# Returns a nested data.table where:
# - name: trait names (adg, bf)
# - data: one row per animal with columns animal, farm1, farm2

# Example 2: numeric indices
r2p_nest(growth, names_from = 2, cols = 3:4, id = 1)
```

```{r tests-r2p_nest}
test_that("r2p_nest aligns records of the same id across levels", {
  d <- data.frame(id = c(1, 1, 2, 2), env = c("A", "B", "A", "B"),
                  t1 = 1:4, t2 = 5:8)
  res <- r2p_nest(d, names_from = "env", cols = c("t1", "t2"), id = "id")
  expect_identical(res$name, c("t1", "t2"))
  expect_identical(as.data.frame(res$data[[1]]),
                   data.frame(id = c(1, 2), A = c(1L, 3L), B = c(2L, 4L)))
  expect_s3_class(r2p_nest(d, "env", "t1", id = "id", out_type = "df")$data[[1]],
                  "data.frame", exact = TRUE)
})

test_that("r2p_nest refuses duplicated id / names_from combinations", {
  d <- data.frame(id = c(1, 1, 2), env = c("A", "A", "B"), t1 = 1:3)
  expect_error(r2p_nest(d, "env", "t1", id = "id"), "uniquely identify")
})

test_that("r2p_nest warns about NA in names_from", {
  d <- data.frame(id = c(1, 1, 2, 2), env = c("a", NA, "a", "b"), y = 1:4)
  expect_warning(res <- r2p_nest(d, names_from = "env", cols = "y", id = "id"), "NA")
  expect_true("NA" %in% names(res$data[[1]]))
})
```
